core_obligations: Disintegrate the rotation invariant probability measure on the unit sphere: the projection dropping u_r gives dmu(u) = (2r-2)/(2pi) dtheta wedge t^{2r-3} dt wedge dmu'(u') with |u_r|^2 = 1-t^2 (eq:measure, lines 1619-1629); homogeneity then yields the two recursion identities labelled 5.10 and 5.10' (lines 1630-1641) and the base moment formulas, obtained by induction on r and p (lines 1642-1647).

Upper bound (a): orthonormal coordinates reduce the integral of |ell(u)|^{2p} to m_{r,p} = p!(r-1)!/(p+r-1)!, and Hoelder's inequality gives I(ell_1,...,ell_p) <= prod_j (int |ell_j|^{2p} dmu)^{1/p} = m_{r,p} prod_j |ell_j|^2, with equality iff all forms are proportional (item 1, lines 1649-1661).

Lower bound (b) by induction on p: choose an orthonormal basis with ell_j(e_r) = 1, split u = u' + u_r e_r, expand prod_j |ell'_j(u') + u_r|^2 through the elementary symmetric functions s_k, average over the phase of u_r (Parseval) and use the beta-type identity (2r-2) int_0^1 t^{2k} (1-t^2)^{p-k} t^{2r-3} dt = (r-1)(k+r-2)!(p-k)!/(p+r-1)! to arrive at the basic inequality on the smaller sphere (eq:basic_inequality, lines 1663-1699).

Induction step: in the normalized case ell_p = <.,e_r> (so ell'_p = 0) the symmetric functions s_k for k <= p-1 are unchanged and s_p = 0, while (p-k)! >= (p-1-k)!, so eq:basic_inequality passes from p-1 to p; the general case follows from U(r)-invariance and the density of tuples with ell_p a coordinate form (lines 1700-1708).

Equality case of (b) by induction on r: split the tuple at e_r into q vanishing and p-q normalized forms, compare the k=0 coefficients for the pairs (p, r) and (p-1, r) to force strictness unless q = p-1, then descend to the case (r-1, p-1), concluding p <= r and pairwise orthogonality (lines 1710-1753).
proof_roadmap: Derive the measure disintegration on the sphere and the two homogeneity recursions.
Prove the sharp upper bound via the moment formula and Hoelder, with the proportionality equality case.
Expand the product into elementary symmetric functions and average over the fiber phase to reduce the lower bound to the basic inequality.
Close the lower bound by induction on p through the coordinate-form case and a density argument.
Settle the equality case by induction on r with the vanishing/non-vanishing split and coefficient comparison.
